The Stratigraphy of a Nation
Criollos & Criollos Nuevos

Molina Enríquez diagnosed Mexico not through its political parties, but through
its sociological strata-distinct biological and cultural groups vying for
survival, compressed by the gravity of history and geography.

The Criollos: A divided aristocracy
Criollos Señores (The Laic Elite)
Descendants of conquerors. Characterized by a
"rural feudalism" and an obsession with pure
bloodlines, aristocratic tradition, and political power.
They held the government but envied the Church's wealth.
Criollos Clero (The Religious Elite)
The upper echelons of the Church. They
controlled vast, highly productive amortized
lands (temporalidades) and massive capital.
The Fatal Flaw
After Independence, these two factions turned on each other in a
war for ultimate supremacy, exhausting their collective strength.

Criollos
Mestizos
The Hybrid Reality
Repugned by Criollos for their

The Psychological Profile

To appease angry Mestizos, the Circular of Oct 9 waived taxes for land valued under 200
pesos, inadvertently targeting Indigenous communal lands. Stripped of access to communal
forests and pastures, they starved and sold their legal titles to Mestizos for pennies or alcohol,
instantly converting peaceful communities into armies of desperate mercenaries.

The untreated illness of the soil
M EX I CO
Molina Enríquez's ultimate warning: The Porfirian peace was a brilliant, artificial feat
of political engineering, but it completely ignored the biological imperative of the
nation. The railways and foreign capital masked a fatal reality: the Fundamental Zone
_Cereals was still locked in sterile, massive Latifundios. With the Mestizos hungry, the
Indigenous starving, and the land undivided, the geological pressure was at its breaking
point. The stage was perfectly set for 1910.
